newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Lyttelton Port optimistic on coal trade.
newsitem.headline: Lyttelton Port optimistic on coal trade.

text.p: The Lyttelton Port Company continues to be optimistic about its coal trade and expects to reach agreement with Coal New Zealand and Tranz Rail on the volume of exports through the port, chief executive David Viles said in the annual report released on Tuesday.
"We are also poised to benefit from the new Rapahoe mine to be opened by Greymouth Coal Ltd," he said.

The port company has already said it will continue plans to develop long-term coal facilities, despite the Coal Corporation lodging resource consent applications to build a 2 km coal-loading jetty at Granity on the West Coast.
Lyttelton handled 1.4m tonnes of West Coast coal during the year, up from 1.2m tonnes the previous year. Coal makes up 52 percent of the port's export tonnage.
Alan Shadwell, who since balance date has retired as the chairman and a director, said in the report that the long-term future for coal shipments through the port are bright.
Increased competitiveness from eight years of reform have lifted cargo volume well beyond natural growth, Mr Shadwell said.
As reported previously, the port company's after-tax profit for the year was $10.46 million.
This was achieved despite the collapse of a major customer, the ABC Line, Mr Shadwell points out in the annual report.
"Cargo potentially lost through its demise surged back in May, and I expect a full recovery and further growth in the 1996-97 year."
